courses.title: Reading charts
courses.goal: See when an axis starts above zero
courses.overview: Four lessons on Reading charts, aimed at See when an axis starts above zero. Study a lesson, then take its quiz.

lessons.title: The axis is part of the argument

sections.label: Concept
sections.text: In Reading charts, the axis tells you what the marks mean. A cropped scale can make a small change look large. Your focus is See when an axis starts above zero.

sections.label: Try
sections.text: Find one chart and write down what each axis measures.

sections.label: Check
sections.text: If you cannot name both axes, you do not know the claim yet.

quiz.prompt: Before you trust a chart, name…
A cropped scale can…
choices: Make a small change look large.
Remove the need for an axis.

quiz.prompt: You do not know the claim yet when…
choices: There are more than two bars.

sections.label: Concept
sections.text: Ask where the vertical axis starts. Zero tells a different story from a start at 90.

sections.label: Try
sections.text: On your chart, write the first labeled value on the vertical axis.

sections.label: Check
sections.text: Say whether that value is zero.

quiz.prompt: The first question about the vertical axis is…
Starting at 90 instead of 0 can…
A scale that starts at zero…

sections.label: Concept
sections.text: Redraw the same points with a vertical axis that starts at zero. The story that survives is the one the data can support.

sections.label: Try
sections.text: Sketch the bars again from zero, keeping their values.

sections.label: Check
sections.text: Did the dramatic gap survive? If it shrank, the crop was doing the work.

quiz.prompt: Redrawing from zero tests…
choices: Whether you can copy the title.
Whether the bars should be horizontal.
Whether the story survives a fair scale.

quiz.prompt: If the dramatic gap shrinks, then…
choices: The crop was doing the work.

quiz.prompt: The story you keep is…
choices: The one that looked largest at first.
The one that survives the redraw.

sections.label: Concept
sections.text: After the redraw, one sentence should say what is still true. That sentence is the chart’s claim.

sections.label: Try
sections.text: Write one sentence about See when an axis starts above zero that stays true when the axis starts at zero.

sections.label: Check
sections.text: If the sentence needs the cropped axis, it is not the claim.

quiz.prompt: The chart’s claim is…
choices: The most alarming gap on the cropped axis.
The sentence that stays true from zero.

quiz.prompt: A sentence that needs the cropped axis…
How many sentences should state the claim?

steps.label: Try

questions.prompt: Which part of a chart is part of the argument?
A vertical axis that does not start at zero can…
choices: Make a small change look large.

questions.prompt: How do you test a dramatic chart?
choices: Redraw the same points from zero.

lessons.title: A loop visits each item once

sections.label: Concept
sections.text: A loop walks a list from the first item to the last. The body runs once for each item, then stops.

sections.label: Try
sections.text: In Python loops, write a loop that prints each word in a short list. Say out loud which word is next before it prints.

sections.label: Check
sections.text: If the list has three words, the body runs three times. Count them.

quiz.prompt: How many times does a loop body run?
choices: Forever, until you close the file.
Once, no matter how long the list is.
Once for each item in the list.

quiz.prompt: A list of three words means the body…
choices: Does not run, because words are text.

quiz.prompt: The loop stops when…
choices: It has visited the last item.

sections.label: Concept
sections.text: An empty list has nothing to visit, so the body never runs. That is the useful part of “Understand an empty list”: no items means no work inside the loop.

sections.label: Try
sections.text: Run the same loop on []. Watch for a print. There should be none.

sections.label: Check
sections.text: Say what you expected, then what happened. If they differ, the empty case is the lesson.

quiz.prompt: What happens when a loop meets an empty list?
choices: The body runs once with a blank item.
Python fills the list for you.

quiz.prompt: Why is the empty list worth testing?
choices: It shows the body is skipped when there is nothing to visit.

quiz.prompt: In this course, “Understand an empty list” points at…
choices: How to sort a long list.
What the loop does when there are no items.

sections.label: Concept
sections.text: The loop variable keeps the last item it was given. If the body never ran, that name was never set by the loop.

sections.label: Try
sections.text: After a loop over three words, print the loop variable. Then try the same after an empty list and notice the difference.

sections.label: Check
sections.text: Guess the value first. Run it second. The guess is the point.

quiz.prompt: After a loop over three words, the loop variable holds…
If the body never ran, the loop variable…
choices: Was not set by the loop.

quiz.prompt: The useful order is…
choices: Run the code, then invent a reason.

lessons.title: Hand the list to a function

sections.label: Concept
sections.text: A function can take the list as a parameter. The loop inside sees that list, not some other list with the same idea.

sections.label: Try
sections.text: Write a function that prints each item. Call it once with words and once with an empty list.

sections.label: Check
sections.text: Point at the parameter and say which list it is on each call.

quiz.prompt: What does the loop inside the function walk?
choices: Only lists that are not empty.
The list that was passed in.

quiz.prompt: Two calls, one with words and one with [], should…
choices: Print the words, then print nothing.

quiz.prompt: You understand the function when you can…
choices: Say which list the parameter holds on each call.
Add more arguments until it looks finished.
